subject: Medicorp inference evaluation — reservation scope & next experiments
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita.rao@medicorp.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Medicorp inference evaluation — reservation scope & next experiments

Hi Anita — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC and the hyperscaler comparison you asked about.

What we heard (pressing priorities)
- 99th percentile latency under 512 tokens is the gating SLA for your user-facing feature.
- Sustained throughput to support peak of ~120 qps for the core embedding/rerank path.
- Deterministic fallbacks during outages (need region-level redundancy).
- Compliance items: SOC 2 report, audit log retention, and KMS integration.

How Redwood differentiates for this evaluation
- Unified runtime: same inference API and rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private — same config works across both tests.
- Cost controls: autorebatching + KV-prefix caching + quantization profiles (we can run with/without to show delta).
- Smart routing & graceful degradation: automated fallback to a lower-cost model variant with preserved output quality; we can simulate a hyperscaler outage and show seamless failover.
- Dedicated guarantees: reserved GPU pools with explicit autoscale thresholds and SLA-backed latency targets (we'll provide the proposed SLO language).

Proposed next tests (please confirm or adjust):
1) Baseline: run your current model on Hyperscaler A and Redwood Dedicated with identical payloads (same tokenization, 512-token cap) for 2 hours during a traffic window we agree. Measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, and total token cost.
2) Stress: sustained 30-minute ramp to 120 qps to validate queuing and autoscale behavior.
3) Failover: simulate a region outage / capacity throttle and verify routing/fallback behavior.
4) Cost delta: quantization + batching on Redwood vs standard hyperscaler config.

Operational asks from Medicorp
- Sample payloads & auth to a staging API endpoint (or a sanitized dataset)
- A technical contact for Luke to coordinate infra/networking questions
- Decision timeline — you mentioned an exec review in mid-October; confirm target date

Attachments I included: Redwood_Dedicated_Playbook_v2.pdf (test matrix + SLO wording) and hyperscaler_comp_matrix.xlsx (feature-by-feature comparison with Hyperscaler A/B). Also included a quick benchmark script (medicorp_sample_benchmark.sh) you can drop into your infra team.

Suggested next steps
- Confirm the test window (I propose 2027-09-20 to 2027-09-21 for the live baseline).
- I’ll schedule a 30–45m technical kickoff with Luke + our infra lead (Grace) — available Tue/Wed next week.

If that plan matches your expectations I’ll lock resources and provision a reserved pool for the Dedicated side (draft numbers below).

Draft reserved pool suggestion (for the POC)
- 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved for 2 weeks) — targeted at your 120 qps sustained requirement.
- Canary burst allowance up to +50% for 1 hour/day to mirror expected traffic spikes.

Thanks — happy to tighten the plan after your notes.

—
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0191
From: Anita Rao <anita.rao@medicorp.com>

Cc: Luke Chen <luke.chen@medicorp.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medicorp inference evaluation — reservation scope & next experiments

Sean — thanks for the thorough recap. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Reserve minimums: what is the minimum commit for a short POC? You suggested 8 GPUs — is there a lower band we can try (we're sensitive to committed spend while exec is still deciding). Also want to understand overage billing and hourly burst pricing.

2) Burst & overprovisioning: you mentioned +50% canary burst — is that billed as on-demand? How do you prioritize burst capacity when Reserved pools and shared capacity overlap?

3) Fallback semantics: if you route to a lower-cost model variant during a capacity event, how do you preserve output quality (can we pin a quality threshold)? Will the logs show model switch events at request level?

4) Compliance: please share the latest SOC 2 snapshot and our options for audit-log retention beyond default retention.

Pricing ballpark would be helpful (order-of-magnitude). If this looks reasonable we'll set up the technical kickoff. Wed next week works for Luke and me for a 45-min deep-dive — are you available 1pm PT?

-Anita
Anita Rao
Director, Platform Engineering | Medicorp
anita.rao@medicorp.com | +1 (415) 555-0138
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita.rao@medicorp.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medicorp inference evaluation — reservation scope & next experiments

Anita — great questions. Quick answers and an updated POC plan.

Reserve minimums and pricing
- POC friendly option: we can provision a 4 GPU reserved pool for a 2-week eval (minimum for reserved pricing is 4 GPUs for short trials).
- Pricing model: reserved monthly rate (pro-rated for the trial) + usage-based token fees. Hourly burst above reserved capacity is billed at the 'burst' rate (we'll share the exact price sheet in the doc I’ll upload).
- Overage handling: if reserved pool saturated, smart routing will attempt burst capacity; if unavailable, requests go to the fallback model variant (we log all switch events).

Burst behavior & capacity prioritization
- Burst capacity is a different allocation and billed separately; customers with Dedicated reserved pools get prioritization over pure on-demand tenants but behind hard SLA commitments (we'll provide the priority table).

Fallback semantics & observability
- Model switch events are recorded request-by-request in the trace (route, model_version, reason).
- We can pin a quality threshold (e.g., maintain >=0.92 ROC-AUC on your reranker test set) and use that as an automated rollback/notification trigger.

Compliance artifacts
- SOC 2 snapshot and audit-log retention options attached in the playbook. For Medicorp we can extend log retention as a paid add-on; details in the doc.

Updated POC plan (confirmed)
- Trial: 2-week POC starting 2027-09-20.
- Reserved pool: 4 GPUs initially (can scale to 8 mid-trial if we need to reproduce higher throughput).
- Baseline & stress tests as previously listed.
- Deliverables: latency/throughput report, cost delta report, failover trace samples, compliance artifacts.

Luke + Grace technical kickoff
- Confirmed: Wed 2027-09-14 13:00 PT. I'll send calendar invite and include the bench run checklist.

I’ll upload the detailed price sheet + a DocuSign draft for a short reserved commitment (so procurement can review).

—
Sean

Subject: Re: Medicorp inference evaluation — reservation scope & next experiments

Looping in a quick commercial note — Anita, appreciate the timeline. A couple internal items so we move quickly: 

- Trial concession: for a two-week reserved POC (4 GPUs) we can offer a one-time introductory discount of 15% on the reserved pool pro-rated for the trial to reduce upfront friction.
- If Medicorp commits to a 6-month reserved contract after the POC at >=8 GPUs we can offer a structured discount and a custom SLO addendum to the contract.

I’ve attached the HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4591) for reference and will circulate a DocuSign short-form for the 2-week reservation so procurement has something tangible to review. Grace — please provision the trial pool once Anita confirms.

Thanks — Jonas
